2026-10-13-DrX-DGM配对交易HJB深度求解.title: DrX-DGM: Solving the Pairs-Trading HJB Variational Inequality with Deep Learning
2026-10-13-DrX-DGM配对交易HJB深度求解.abstract: This report applies the Deep Galerkin Method (DGM) to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman variational inequality of an optimal pairs-trading problem (Tie, Zhang & Zhang, 2017), whose free boundary - the entry and exit thresholds of the trade - is known in closed form: k1 = 1.038 and k2 = 1.283 under the paper's Target/Walmart calibration. A NumPy multilayer perceptron with hand-coded backpropagation is trained for 8,000 iterations on randomly sampled collocation points, with no mesh and no labeled data. The learned value surface is smooth and qualitatively correct, but the trading boundaries extracted from its curvature peaks (1.341 and 1.411) deviate from the closed form by 29.1% and 9.9%. The diagnosis is structural: a smooth network rounds off the kink that the smooth-fit conditions place exactly at the free boundary. The exercise provides a reproducible baseline for neural PDE solvers in stochastic control, and a caution on reading decision boundaries off smooth approximators.

2026-10-13-DrX-闭式解验证配对交易Smooth-Fit数值求解.title: DrX-Verification Report: Numerical Solution of the Smooth-Fit System for Pairs Trading
2026-10-13-DrX-闭式解验证配对交易Smooth-Fit数值求解.abstract: Before trusting a neural-network solver, its benchmark must itself be verified. This technical report independently reproduces the closed-form solution reported in Section 6 of Tie, Zhang & Zhang (2017) for optimal pairs trading under geometric Brownian motion. Starting from the paper's Target/Walmart calibration (drifts 0.2059 and 0.2459, correlation structure and a proportional transaction cost K = 0.001), the value function is reduced to a one-dimensional problem in the price ratio, and the entry and exit thresholds are obtained by solving the smooth-fit algebraic system to full precision: k1 = 1.038 and k2 = 1.283, matching the paper's rounded values 1.039 and 1.282. Every intermediate quantity - the reduced volatility, the characteristic roots and the constants of the general solution - is derived and cross-checked. The verified solution serves as the exact reference against which the companion DGM study measures its approximation error.

2026-10-14-DrX-100万组合模拟仓.title: DrX-A CNY 1 Million Simulated Portfolio
2026-10-14-DrX-100万组合模拟仓.abstract: This page documents a CNY 1,000,000 simulated portfolio that runs three independent strategy sleeves side by side. A CNY 300,000 sleeve trades Xinjinlu (000510.SZ) under the mechanical box-regression rule set; a CNY 400,000 value sleeve tracks six industry leaders for pullback entries; and a CNY 300,000 trend sleeve scans seven semiconductor and AI-theme names for right-side breakouts. Each sleeve keeps its own budget, signals and risk limits, and the combined book is marked to market every trading day with an interactive candlestick-style equity curve. In the current phase the value and trend sleeves record signals and valuations without auto-executing, so the page functions as an auditable lab notebook: every rule is stated in advance, every signal is logged, and performance can be attributed sleeve by sleeve. The design goal is discipline under drawdowns - position size and exits are decided by pre-committed formulas, not by intraday sentiment.

2026-10-14-DrX-新金路箱体回归模拟交易.title: DrX-Box-Regression Simulated Trading on Xinjinlu
2026-10-14-DrX-新金路箱体回归模拟交易.abstract: A CNY 300,000 virtual account trades a single stock, Xinjinlu (000510.SZ), under a fully mechanical box-regression rule set, updated every trading day at 17:00. The trading box is rebuilt daily from robust quantiles of the last 180 sessions and combined with a regression channel: the account buys only in the lowest quarter of the box, at a limit price on the lower edge, in two steps (a 60% probe tranche and a 40% confirmation tranche). Position size follows a regime matrix over channel direction and box quality; the hard stop is set by the smaller of one ATR and 20% of the box height, and both the stop and a three-step take-profit ladder (30/40/30 across the box) are locked at entry and never revised. Gap protection cancels unfilled orders after a low opening beyond 1.50%. The page is the live log of the experiment - signals, fills, equity curve and the dated box chart - with no discretionary override.

2026-11-03-DrX-把最大亏损写成常数.title: DrX-Writing the Maximum Loss as a Constant: The Box-Regression Rulebook and Two Live Rounds
2026-11-03-DrX-把最大亏损写成常数.abstract: This article is the complete rulebook, and the worked demonstration, of the box-regression system that trades Xinjinlu (000510.SZ) in the simulated account. Nine formulas govern the strategy end to end: the robust-quantile trading box and regression channel, the box-position signal (buy at or below 0.25, sell at or above 0.75), the regime-based position matrix, two-step entry at the lower edge with a one-cent penetration fill rule and 1.50% gap protection, the locked hard stop set by the smaller of one ATR and 20% of box height, and a three-step take-profit ladder. Their consequence is an identity: the maximum loss of a round is fixed at order time as shares times stop distance plus fees - a constant, not a random variable. Two live rounds verify the arithmetic: the first closed on the locked stop with a realized loss of CNY -7,608.88, exactly the precomputed cap; the second was open at publication.

2026-10-12-低买高卖的随机优化方法.title: Stochastic Optimization for Buying Low and Selling High: A Model-Free Stochastic Approximation Strategy
2026-10-12-低买高卖的随机优化方法.abstract: How low is low enough to buy, and how high is high enough to sell? Zhang & Zhang (2008) answered analytically for a mean-reverting asset, but their solution needs the model. Song, Yin & Zhang (2009, Stochastic Analysis and Applications) remove that requirement: assuming only mean reversion and no specific price dynamics, they learn the optimal buy and sell thresholds directly from observed prices with a stochastic approximation algorithm, a recursive update that needs no model calibration and no offline optimization. The article explains the construction of the algorithm, why its gain sequence and projection keep it stable, and the convergence argument showing the iterates track the optimal thresholds. Empirical tests on Walmart and IBM price series illustrate the learned rules in action. The piece is a useful counterpoint to the closed-form literature: when the model is unknown or misspecified, a provably convergent learning rule can replace derivation altogether.

2026-10-12-可切换均值回归最优交易规则.title: Optimal Trading under a Switchable Mean-Reversion Model: Threshold Solutions for Buying Low and Selling High
2026-10-12-可切换均值回归最优交易规则.abstract: Classical buy-low-sell-high results assume the equilibrium level of a mean-reverting asset never moves. Nguyen, Tie & Zhang (2014, Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications) let it jump exactly once: the price first oscillates around an old equilibrium, then, at an unannounced random time, around a new one - the step pattern produced by an earnings shock, a policy shift or a changed industry outlook. The trader must therefore solve two coupled problems: trade optimally within each regime, and carry the right position across the jump. The value functions satisfy a system of quasi-variational inequalities, and the optimal strategy remains a threshold rule, with the buy and sell levels in each regime given in closed form through algebraic equations. This study walks through the model, the verification argument and the comparative statics - how jump intensity and the distance between equilibria move the thresholds - and discusses where step-wise equilibria appear in real markets.

2026-10-12-均值回归双阈值解析解.title: Buying Low and Selling High in a Mean-Reverting Market: The Analytic Two-Threshold Rule
2026-10-12-均值回归双阈值解析解.abstract: Zhang & Zhang (2008, Automatica) gave the buy-low-sell-high problem its first fully rigorous treatment. Earlier work had solved only the selling side; the buying side - when to enter a mean-reverting asset - had no rigorous analysis. Using dynamic programming, the authors characterize the value function through a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman quasi-variational inequality and prove that the optimal strategy is a two-threshold rule: buy when the price falls to x1, sell when it rises to x2, and do nothing in between. Better still, the thresholds are not implicit PDE objects - smooth-fit conditions reduce their determination to two quasi-algebraic equations that can be solved numerically in milliseconds. This article unpacks the model (an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck price with proportional transaction costs), the free-boundary structure of the solution, the verification theorem, and the sensitivity of the thresholds to mean-reversion speed, volatility and cost - the reference point for the whole optimal-trading-rule literature that followed.

2026-10-12-均值回归四阈值交易规则.title: Mean-Reversion Trading with Short Selling and Slippage: The Four-Threshold Optimal Rule
2026-10-12-均值回归四阈值交易规则.abstract: Kong & Zhang (2010, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems - Series B) extend the two-threshold buy-low-sell-high rule of Zhang & Zhang (2008) in the two directions practice demands: short selling and execution slippage. The trader may now hold long, flat or short positions in a mean-reverting asset, and every trade pays both a proportional cost and a slippage term. The dynamic programming formulation leads to a quasi-variational inequality whose solution has a four-threshold structure: a buy-to-cover level and a short-entry level on the short side, mirrored by a long-entry and a take-profit level on the long side, with a no-trade band in the middle. Smooth-fit conditions again collapse the free-boundary problem into four quasi-algebraic equations. The study explains the geometry of the four regions, how slippage widens the no-trade band, and why the two-threshold rule is recovered when shorting is banned - a clean view of how constraints reshape optimal trading rules.

2026-10-12-股票质押贷款定价.title: Pricing Stock Loans: A Closed-Form Solution under a Regime-Switching Mean-Reverting Model
2026-10-12-股票质押贷款定价.abstract: A stock loan - cash borrowed against pledged shares, with the borrower free to walk away if the price falls - is economically a European call option on the pledged stock. Prager & Zhang (2010, Journal of Systems Science and Complexity) price it in the setting practitioners actually face: finite maturity, and a share price that switches once between a geometric Brownian (trending) regime and a mean-reverting (range-bound) regime, capturing the way a stock alternates between momentum and consolidation over a loan's life. The article explains the contract mechanics (loan amount, service fee, redemption price growing at the lending rate), derives the closed-form valuation across the two regimes, and examines how the loan value and the implied safe lending ratio respond to volatility, mean-reversion speed, maturity and the switching intensity. A final section discusses the relevance to China's large stock-pledge market, where margin-call spirals in falling markets made exactly these parameters a systemic concern.

2026-10-12-配对交易最优策略.title: An Optimal Strategy for Pairs Trading under Geometric Brownian Motion: Closed-Form Solution, Backtest and Market Prospects
2026-10-12-配对交易最优策略.abstract: Pairs trading is usually built on a mean-reverting spread. Tie, Zhang & Zhang (2017, Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications) drop that crutch: both legs follow geometric Brownian motions, so the spread itself does not revert, and yet an optimal market-neutral strategy still exists in closed form. Formulating the trade as an optimal switching problem over the price ratio, the authors derive explicit entry and exit thresholds from the smooth-fit system, with the strategy's value function given analytically in each region. The empirical section calibrates the model to Target and Walmart and reports a fifteen-year out-of-sample backtest. This study presents the model reduction to the one-dimensional ratio process, the structure of the four trading regions, and the backtest evidence, then assesses what the result means for practice: profitability comes from the optimally timed exploitation of relative drift and volatility, not from an assumed gravitational pull in the spread.

2026-10-12-配对交易最优规则与止损.title: An Optimal Pairs-Trading Rule: Mean-Reverting Spread, Three Thresholds and a Stop-Loss Constraint
2026-10-12-配对交易最优规则与止损.abstract: Entry rules for pairs trading are well studied; the exit that practitioners care most about - the stop-loss - is not. Song & Zhang (2013, Automatica), the prequel to the 2017 GBM treatment by the same group, keep a mean-reverting (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck) spread and, for the first time in this literature, impose the stop-loss level as an explicit state constraint inside the optimal stopping problem. The optimal rule is characterized by three thresholds: enter when the spread is wide enough, take profit when it normalizes, and cut the position unconditionally if the spread dives through the stop level first. The article lays out the problem's motivation from practice - risk limits, margin and model failure - the quasi-variational formulation, and how the constrained solution differs from the unconstrained one: the entry threshold tightens because a trade that can be stopped out must promise more. Numerical sections trace the thresholds as volatility, reversion speed and the stop level vary.

2026-10-12-配对交易综述解读.title: Statistical Arbitrage Pairs Trading: A Review of Krauss (2015) and Outlook
2026-10-12-配对交易综述解读.abstract: Krauss (2015) is among the most cited surveys of pairs trading, reviewing more than ninety papers and organizing the field into five schools: the distance method, cointegration approaches, time-series models, stochastic control, and a residual category including copulas and machine learning. This study works through the survey school by school - the formation and trading periods, the canonical references (Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst's distance method, with reported returns around 11% per year, is the benchmark), and Krauss's assessment of what each approach can and cannot deliver - then turns to the survey's forward-looking questions: declining profitability as the strategy crowds, the role of transaction costs and short-sale constraints, high-frequency implementations, and extensions from pairs to baskets and full multivariate statistical arbitrage. It closes with our own outlook on where the stochastic-control branch of the literature - the branch most of this column's readings come from - is heading.

2026-10-13-DGM求解高维偏微分方程的深度学习算法.title: DGM: A Deep Learning Algorithm for Solving High-Dimensional Partial Differential Equations
2026-10-13-DGM求解高维偏微分方程的深度学习算法.abstract: Finite differences need O(h^-(d+1)) grid points in d spatial dimensions, so classical solvers die in high dimensions. Sirignano & Spiliopoulos (2018) propose the Deep Galerkin Method (DGM): a deep neural network approximates the PDE solution, and stochastic gradient descent trains it on randomly sampled space-time points to satisfy the differential operator, the initial condition and the boundary conditions simultaneously - no mesh anywhere, which is what makes problems with up to 200 dimensions tractable. This article explains the architecture (a gated, LSTM-like layer structure suited to sequential dependence), the least-squares loss over the PDE residual, and the paper's approximation theorem for a class of quasilinear parabolic equations. The numerical evidence spans high-dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations, Burgers' equation and the free-boundary PDE of an American option. DGM is the methodological backbone of this site's own pairs-trading experiment, where its solution is benchmarked against a verified closed form.

2026-10-13-动态配对交易的随机控制显式解.title: Dynamic Pairs Trading: An Explicit Optimal Strategy via Stochastic Control
2026-10-13-动态配对交易的随机控制显式解.abstract: Tourin & Yan (2013, Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control) recast pairs trading as a Merton portfolio problem: the investor holds a riskless account and two cointegrated stocks and maximizes expected exponential utility of terminal wealth. Unlike earlier stochastic-control treatments, the two legs need not be traded in equal and opposite amounts - the optimal dollar-neutral-violating positions are part of the solution. The paper's central result is a dimension reduction: under exponential utility, the high-dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation collapses to a one-dimensional linear parabolic PDE, from which the optimal holdings follow in closed form as functions of the spread and time. This study presents the reduction step by step, interprets the optimal position as a mean-reversion bet scaled by risk aversion and horizon, and reviews the empirical illustration on minute-level Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan data - a bridge between the threshold-rule literature and continuous portfolio choice.

2026-10-13-配对交易最优随机控制与库存惩罚.title: Stochastic Optimal Control of Pairs Trading: Trading Rules under Absolute and Relative Inventory Penalties
2026-10-13-配对交易最优随机控制与库存惩罚.abstract: Threshold rules trade in all-or-nothing steps; real desks trade continuously and hate carrying inventory. Al-Aradi (2015, University of Toronto) formulates pairs trading as a continuous stochastic control problem in which the trader chooses execution rates for two cointegrated assets subject to linear instantaneous price impact, and is charged for the inventory she carries - in two distinct ways: an absolute penalty on the total position, and a relative penalty on the imbalance between the legs. Three cases are solved: one requires numerical work, while the two penalty structures with tractable scaling yield closed-form optimal trading rates. Using a simulated trading system, the study maps how the optimal speed and the profit distribution respond to transaction and liquidation costs, the penalty-aversion coefficients and the speed of mean reversion. The article explains the formulation and reads the two closed-form solutions as a spectrum between pure spread speculation and inventory-averse market making.

2026-10-13-高维均值回归篮子期权近似定价.title: Approximate Pricing of Basket Options on High-Dimensional Mean-Reverting Assets
2026-10-13-高维均值回归篮子期权近似定价.abstract: A basket option on mean-reverting underlyings - energy, rates, commodities - has no closed-form price, and Monte Carlo is too slow for routine use, worse in high dimensions. Li & Wu (2008, Computers & Operations Research) propose a two-step approximation: moment matching first replaces the high-dimensional basket by a one-dimensional process with matched first two moments, and a Black-Scholes-type formula then prices the option on that surrogate in closed form. Across 2, 4, 6 and 10 dimensions and three mean-reverting models (including exponential Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics), the approximation stays within 1% of Monte Carlo while taking roughly one ten-thousandth of the computing time - and, remarkably, its runtime does not grow with dimension. This study explains why the basket of mean-reverting assets is close enough to lognormal for moment matching to work, where the approximation deteriorates (deep out-of-the-money, long maturities), and what the trick teaches about taming the curse of dimensionality by structure rather than by computation.

2026-11-03-DrX-HJ方程到BS方程.title: DrX-From the Hamilton-Jacobi Equation to Black-Scholes: A Variational-Calculus Research Program, Lecture 1
2026-11-03-DrX-HJ方程到BS方程.abstract: Lecture 1 of a study series that rebuilds mathematical finance on the variational calculus of Zhang Gongqing's Lectures on the Calculus of Variations. The lecture asks a single question: where does the Black-Scholes equation actually come from? Starting from the deterministic Hamilton-Jacobi equation of classical mechanics, it lifts the problem to finance by dynamic programming under geometric Brownian motion: Ito's lemma turns the Bellman principle into the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, the delta-hedging argument identifies the generalized momentum with the hedge ratio and eliminates the drift, and the Black-Scholes PDE falls out - with the Feynman-Kac formula closing the loop back to a probabilistic representation. A term-by-term table maps every object of the derivation onto its variational counterpart (value function, momentum, Legendre transform), setting up the series' three-stage plan: classical variational methods and duality, stochastic variational methods and large deviations, and optimal control. Exercises point to the Legendre duality developed later in the course.

2026-11-03-DrX-变分法学习路径与策略实现规划.title: DrX-A Study Path for Variational Calculus in Financial Mathematics: Three Books, Four Stages and an Implementation Plan
2026-11-03-DrX-变分法学习路径与策略实现规划.abstract: This is the roadmap for a self-study programme that connects three books: Zhang Gongqing's Lectures on the Calculus of Variations as the skeleton (it poses the problems), Oksendal's Stochastic Differential Equations as the toolbox (it supplies the rigorous language), and Nualart's Malliavin Calculus as the lift to infinite dimensions (differentiation on Wiener space, whose integration-by-parts formula computes Greeks without differentiating the payoff). The path runs in four stages of roughly three weeks each - classical variational methods and duality; stochastic analysis foundations; stochastic control and dual pricing; stochastic variational methods and extreme risk - each with an explicit pass criterion. Attached is an engineering plan of five milestones that turns the theory into running, simulated systems on this site: an HJB variational-inequality solver, a Malliavin-weight Greeks and hedging engine, a pairs-trading HJB simulation, a large-deviation risk gauge for the tracked stock universe, and a constrained portfolio solver - each shipped small, benchmarked, and subordinated to the existing trading discipline.

2026-11-03-DrX-美式期权变分不等式与自由边界.title: DrX-Lecture Example: Variational Inequalities and Free Boundaries for American Options - the Obstacle-Problem Isomorphism and the Perpetual American Put in Closed Form
2026-11-03-DrX-美式期权变分不等式与自由边界.abstract: An American option is an obstacle problem: the value function is a membrane held above the payoff obstacle, in contact where exercise is optimal and free where it is not. This lecture develops that isomorphism rigorously - from the dynamic programming principle through the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman variational inequality and its linear complementarity form, min(-Vt - L V, V - payoff) = 0, to viscosity solutions, the Snell envelope, and the two classical solution technologies, variational methods and penalty approximation. The worked example solves the perpetual American put in closed form: with gamma = 2r/sigma^2, value matching and smooth pasting give the exercise boundary S* = 2rK/(2r + sigma^2) and the value V = (K - S*)(S/S*)^(-gamma) in the holding region. For r = 5%, sigma = 20% and K = 100, S* = 71.43 and V(100) = 12.32. This closed form is adopted as the acceptance benchmark for the numerical HJB solver built later in the series.

2026-11-06-SGu-双基金核心卫星模拟仓.title: SGu Core-Satellite Dual-Fund Portfolio: Daily Simulation Record
2026-11-06-SGu-双基金核心卫星模拟仓.abstract: This page is the daily operating record of a CNY 1,000,000 simulated core-satellite portfolio built for SGu: 70% in China Merchants Quantitative Selection Fund (001917) and 30% in Yongying Technology Select Fund (022364), with the two sleeves accounted independently. A rotating operation card at the top states the current positions, the orders to be executed at the next published NAV, and the trigger levels for the day. Below it, a brief rule summary is followed by the current status of both sleeves, the latest indicator charts, and a dated log of every signal, trade and equity reading since inception. The design rationale, mathematical models, complete rule set and backtest are documented in the companion theory article; this page records execution only.

2026-11-06-SGu-双基金策略设计与回测.title: SGu Core-Satellite Dual-Fund Strategy: Design, Mathematical Models and Backtest
2026-11-06-SGu-双基金策略设计与回测.abstract: This article documents the design of a CNY 1,000,000 simulated core-satellite portfolio for SGu, allocating 70% to China Merchants Quantitative Selection Fund (001917) and 30% to Yongying Technology Select Fund (022364). The core fund, whose detrended cumulative NAV is modelled as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, is traded with a level-triggered Z-score state machine (100% below -2.5 sigma, 80% below -1.8 sigma, 30% above +2.0 sigma, 60% near the mean), guarded by an alpha filter and a CSI 500 circuit breaker. The satellite fund, modelled as a jump-diffusion, is traded with right-side momentum, a -12% drawdown cut and a hard MA60 exit. Portfolio variance is decomposed with an Euler risk attribution, and a two-year backtest on real NAV data with fund-schedule FIFO fees shows the combined state machines reducing maximum drawdown from -34.61% to -17.84% versus buy-and-hold.

2026-11-07-DrX-变分学讲义第一讲.title: DrX-Zhang Gongqing's Lectures on the Calculus of Variations, Lecture 1: Variational Problems and Functionals - Ten Examples and the Road to Stochastic Variational Calculus
2026-11-07-DrX-变分学讲义第一讲.abstract: This is the first instalment of a lecture-by-lecture reading of Zhang Gongqing's Lectures on the Calculus of Variations, written for senior undergraduates in mathematics with full derivations and added explanations wherever the original text moves quickly. Lecture 1 poses no equations; it defines the object of study - a functional I : M -> R on a set of admissible functions - including the instructive non-example I4(u) = f(u(x)), and lays out ten examples as problem templates: the brachistochrone, geodesics, minimal surfaces, eigenvalue problems and best constants in inequalities via the Rayleigh quotient, the vibrating plate, an optimal-control problem of reinvestment solved in full (a bang-bang strategy switching at T - 1/alpha), Mumford-Shah image segmentation, harmonic maps, the Hamiltonian action as a critical value, and the Einstein-Hilbert action. A synthesis section integrates the companion texts: Oksendal's expectation functionals, adapted controls and value function, with a term-by-term match between Zhang's reinvestment example and Oksendal's optimal portfolio problem, and Nualart's Malliavin derivative as the first variation transported to Wiener space, anchored by the Gaussian integration-by-parts formula whose one-dimensional case is Stein's lemma. All claims carry explicit citations to the three books.

2026-11-07-DrX-变分学讲义第二讲.title: DrX-Zhang Gongqing's Lectures on the Calculus of Variations, Lecture 2: The Euler-Lagrange Equation - First Variation, the du Bois-Reymond Lemma and Four Solvable Cases
2026-11-07-DrX-变分学讲义第二讲.abstract: Lecture 2 of the reading of Zhang Gongqing's Lectures on the Calculus of Variations derives the first necessary condition for an extremum. Starting from the finite-dimensional Fermat argument - restrict to a line, use that a one-variable minimum forces equality in the two-sided limit - the article computes the first variation of I(u) = integral of L(t, u, u') dt and notes Zhang's distinctive step: integrate the L_u term, not the L_p term, by parts, so that no differentiability of the minimizer is assumed in advance. The du Bois-Reymond lemma then converts the integral identity into the Euler-Lagrange equation in integral form, with the differential form and the Lipschitz and piecewise-C1 extensions discussed. Natural boundary conditions for free endpoints follow from the same first variation. The four solvable cases (L independent of u, of t, of p, and coordinate changes) are worked in full: Newton's equations and the geodesic equation with Christoffel symbols, the cycloid for the brachistochrone, the catenary for the minimal surface of revolution, great circles on the sphere, and straight lines via polar coordinates. Companion readings identify the stochastic counterparts: Oksendal's HJB(I) theorem as the random version of 'first variation equals zero', and Nualart's divergence operator, defined by duality through the integration-by-parts formula, as the Wiener-space form of the du Bois-Reymond extraction argument.

2026-11-07-DrX-变分学讲义第三讲.title: DrX-Zhang Gongqing's Lectures on the Calculus of Variations, Lecture 3: The Second Variation, the Legendre-Hadamard Condition, Jacobi Fields and Conjugate Points
2026-11-07-DrX-变分学讲义第三讲.abstract: Lecture 3 of the reading of Zhang Gongqing's Lectures on the Calculus of Variations answers the question Lecture 2 left open: satisfying the Euler-Lagrange equation is only necessary, so when is an extremal actually a minimizer? The article develops the second variation as the Hessian of the functional, stating the abstract pair of conditions - positive semi-definiteness is necessary, and a coercive lower bound delta2 I >= lambda integral of (|phi|^2 + |phi'|^2) is sufficient - with the proof idea that quantitative positivity survives small perturbations. A spike-shaped family of test functions extracts the pointwise part, the Legendre-Hadamard condition on L_pp, and Poincare's inequality (with a remark on its sharp constant pi^2) rewrites the sufficient condition in terms of phi' alone; an example shows pointwise positivity of the full block matrix is not necessary, because on short intervals Poincare still saves positivity - the exact threshold is the first conjugate point. Treating the second variation as a variational problem in its own right produces the accessory functional, the Jacobi equation and the Jacobi operator; conjugate points are defined as zeros of nontrivial Jacobi fields, their interior existence rules out minimality, and for geodesics on a surface they are computed from the Gauss curvature (first conjugate point at pi/sqrt(K)). For scalar problems a positive Jacobi field completes the square via the Jacobi identity and yields a full sufficient condition. Counterparts in the companion books: Oksendal's verification theorem (HJB II) as a global-form sufficient condition, the linear regulator as the case where second-order positivity is automatic via the Riccati equation, and Nualart's Ornstein-Uhlenbeck generator L = -delta D, a second-order self-adjoint operator whose chaos spectrum 0, -1, -2, ... is completely explicit.
